title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 29 (Decision making by panel of arbitrators)

content.overview: Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, in arbitral proceedings with more than one arbitrator, any decision of the tribunal shall be made by a majority of all its members. Questions of procedure may be decided by the presiding arbitrator if so authorised by the parties or all the members of the tribunal.
content.glance: Majority decision unless agreed otherwise; presiding arbitrator may decide procedure if authorised.
content.study: Default rule is majority of all members. Parties may agree otherwise. The presiding arbitrator may decide questions of procedure if authorised by the parties or by all members of the tribunal.

sections.heading: Majority rule
sections.body: Unless otherwise agreed, any decision is made by a majority of all members.

sections.heading: Presiding arbitrator on procedure
sections.body: May decide questions of procedure if authorised by the parties or all members.

provisions.title: Decision making by panel of arbitrators

questionsAndAnswers.question: How are decisions made by a multi-member tribunal under section 29?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: By a majority of all its members, unless the parties agree otherwise. Procedure may be decided by the presiding arbitrator if authorised.

examTips: Majority default; procedure may be delegated to presiding arbitrator if authorised.

enhancement.definition: Section 29 governs decision-making by a panel of arbitrators.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Majority decision unless agreed otherwise; presiding arbitrator may decide procedure if authorised.
